_comment: Story 25.14: the Villager's Voice, the ambient Social Mirror (narrative-design.md). Overheard, never addressed; tonal dial GENTLE: rueful and questioning, never accusatory, in-world terms only (the Crown, the lords, the Guild). Registers escalate; weights are relative and Epic 10.4 (Hidden Threshold) may reweight them from game state. Every line must rhyme with a pillar, or it's cut.

lines: Three new taxes this year and the road still washes out every spring. Where's it all going?
The Mages' Guild eats first, drinks first, never pays the toll. Funny, that.
The lord's men counted my geese twice this month. The geese didn't enjoy it either.
Bread's dearer every market day. The loaves aren't getting any bigger.
They mended the lord's bridge in a week. The mill road's been rutted since my father's time.
Tithe, toll, tax. I'd pay a coin to hear a word that doesn't start with a T.
Rain on the wheat again. Still, the Crown will want its share, wet or dry.
Another guild banner over the tavern. Watch — they'll send our boys off and call the dead ones 'heroes.'
Easy to be brave when it's someone else walking out the gate.
The Hendry boy signed on up the hill. His mother still sets a place for him.
They ring a bell up there when one doesn't come back. You stop counting, after a while.
Heroes, the songs say. My brother only wanted to see the sea.
Why does the Chronicle always know what'll happen before it happens? Who writes that thing, really?
Is there a hand behind all this? …Course there is. There always is.
That hourglass up at the tavern. The sand never runs out. Have you noticed? Never.
My gran said there was a guild on that hill before the guild on that hill. And one before that.
Tall fellow in a mask walked the market at dawn. Nobody saw him come. Nobody saw him go.
